title: PSA Profischule Campus - Haus A - Bodenbelagsarbeiten Betonwerkstein
description: Die Profilschule bildet mit der Mensa und der Sporthalle sowie den Sportanlagen das Schulzentrum. Es wurde zwischen den Jahren 1963 und 1971 erbaut, mehrfach erweitert und lange Zeit von einer Realschule genutzt. Mit dem Auslaufen der Realschule am 31.7.2016 nutzt die neue Schulform (Profilschule) die ehemaligen Gebäude. Um den Profilschulstandort in Ascheberg zu konzentrieren, wird die ehem. Hauptschule in Herben aufgegeben. Dafür müssen die Bestandsgebäude erweitert, umgebaut und saniert werden. Der neue Standort wird aus drei Gebäuden bestehen (Haus A (2), Haus B (3) und Haus C (1)) plus einem Wirtschaftsgebäude in leichter Bauweise. Haus A (2) wird nach Abschluss der Maßnahme ein saniertes Bestandsgebäude sein, Haus C (1) und Haus B (3) jeweils ein Neubau.

title: Sanierung Schwimmbad Revierpark Vonderort - Freianlagenplanung Los 2
description: Der Revierpark Vonderort, Bottroper Straße 350, Oberhausen, entstand 1974 als dritter von insgesamt fünf Revierparks im Ruhrgebiet und wurde zusammen mit dem dortigen Schwimmbad eröffnet. Die Badelandschaft wurde in den 90er Jahren zum Solebad Vonderort umgestaltet und später um die Saunalandschaft erweitert. Das Solebad ist wegen des nicht mehr nutzbaren Solebeckens seit August 2019 außer Betrieb. Seitdem ist das Solebad geschlossen. Die Bausubstanz der Badanlage weist altersbedingt erhebliche Mängel auf und ist sanierungsbedürftig. Die Stadt hat sich an dem Projektaufruf des Bundesprogramms "Sanierung kommunaler Einrichtungen in Bereichen Sport, Jugend, und Kultur" 2023 des Bundesministeriums für Wohnen, Stadtentwicklung und Bauwesen mit dem Projekt "Sanierung und Erweiterung des Hallenbades im Revierpark Vonderort in Oberhausen" beteiligt. Gegenstand der vorliegenden Ausschreibung ist die Planung von Freianlagen gemäß § 39 HOAI i. V. m. Anlage 11 Nr. 11.1 zur HOAI.

title: Betonsanierungsarbeiten
description: In der Förderschule des Caritas Förderzentrums St. Laurentius und Paulus in der Queichheimer Hauptstraße 235 in Landau i.d. Pfalz werden zwei Drittel der derzeit 160 Schüler im Bildungsgang ganzheitliche Entwicklung unterrichtet, d. h. neben dem Förderschwerpunkt motorische Entwicklung besteht auch noch sonderpädagogischer Förderbedarf im Bereich ganzheitliche Entwicklung. Die Förderschule wurde im Jahr 1971 in Massivbauweise als Flachdachgebäude erbaut. 1990 wurde ein komplettes Walmdach aufgesetzt. Der Dachraum ist ungenutzt. Seither haben sich die (sonder-) pädagogischen Anforderungen an das Schulgebäude und die Einrichtung weitreichend verändert. Da beim Bau der Schule, damals für ca. 120 Schülerinnen und Schüler geplant, die heute gültigen pädagogischen Konzepte nicht berücksichtigt werden konnten und in den vergangenen Jahren keine größeren Maßnahmen durchgeführt wurden, befindet sich die Schule nicht mehr auf dem aktuellen Stand. Somit werden die Durchführungen umfassender Baumaßnahmen am bestehenden Schulgebäude geplant. In den vergangenen Jahren wurden lediglich umfassende Brandschutzmaßnahmen sowie die Sanierung des Trinkwasseranlage des Gesamteinrichtung durchgeführt. Die Maßnahmen dieser Sanierung sind wie folgt geplant: Grundlegende Sanierungsmaßnahmen in Klassenräumen, Therapieräumen, Büros und Fluren Einbau einer Lüftungsanlage inklusive Einbau von Klimatisierungsgeräten Erneuerung von elektrischen Leitungsführungen Sanierung des Schwimmbades mit Umkleiden Sanierung der Aula und WC-Anlagen Sanierung der Pflegebäder, WC-Anlagen Umbau der Lehrküche Herstellung eines barrierefreien Pausenhofes Die Gebäudeteile, welche Gegenstand dieser Maßnahme sind, beinhalten folgende Nutzungen: Bauteil P: - UG (Teilunterkellerung): Schwimmbadbecken – Schwimmbadtechnik - EG: Schwimmbad mit zugehörigen Umkleiden, Klassen-, Therapie- und Verwaltungsräume, kleinere Sanitärbereiche - OG: Klassen-, Therapie- und Verwaltungsräume, großer Sanitärbereich für die Schüler*innen - Dachraum: Einbau einer Technikzentrale, Leitungsverzug der neuen Lüftungsanlage Bauteil R: - EG: Großküche (NICHT Gegenstand dieser Maßnahme) - OG: Mensa, Ausgabeküche, Klassen-, Therapie- und Verwaltungsräume - Dachraum: ungenutzt – lediglich Leitungsverzug der neuen Lüftungsanlage Bauteil O: - EG: Notwendiger Flur, Erschließung, Verwaltungsräume - OG: Notwendiger Flur, kleine Sanitärbereiche, Erschließung, Verwaltungsräume - Dachraum: ungenutzt – lediglich Leitungsverzug der neuen Lüftungsanlage Bauteil A: - EG: Gymnastikhalle mit zugehörigen Nebenräumen, Klassen-, Therapie- und Verwaltungsräume, großer Sanitärbereich für die Schüler*innen, Werkraum, Lehrküche - OG: Klassen-, Therapie- und Verwaltungsräume, großer Sanitärbereich für die Schüler*innen - Dachraum: Einbau einer Technikzentrale, Leitungsverzug der neuen Lüftungsanlage Bauteil B: - EG: Ambulanter Dienst Verwaltungsräume (NICHT Gegenstand dieser Maßnahme), Haupteingang - OG: Klassenräume, kleiner Sanitärbereich - Dachraum: ungenutzt – lediglich Leitungsverzug der neuen Lüftungsanlage Bauteil C: - EG: Klassen-, Therapie- und Verwaltungsräume, kleiner Sanitärbereich, Erschließung - OG 1: (NICHT Gegenstand dieser Maßnahme), Erschließung - OG 2: (NICHT Gegenstand dieser Maßnahme), Erschließung - OG 3: (NICHT Gegenstand dieser Maßnahme), Erschließung - OG 4: Klassen- und Therapieräume, kleiner Sanitärbereich, Erschließung - Dachraum: Einbau einer Technikzentrale Bauteil L: - EG: Notwendiger Flur, Erschließung, Rampe - OG: Notwendiger Flur, Erschließung, Rampe - Dachraum: ungenutzt – lediglich Leitungsverzug der neuen Lüftungsanlage Bauteil M: - EG: Notwendiger Flur, Erschließung, Rampe - OG: (NICHT Gegenstand dieser Maßnahme) - Dachraum: ungenutzt (NICHT Gegenstand dieser Maßnahme) Bauteil F: - EG: Aula mit Bühne, Sanitärbereich - OG: (NICHT Gegenstand dieser Maßnahme) - Dachraum: ungenutzt (NICHT Gegenstand dieser Maßnahme) Diese Gebäudeteile sind NICHT Gegenstand der Maßnahme: Bauteil D, Bauteil E, Bauteil U, Bauteil G, Bauteil N, Bauteil K, Bauteil H, Bauteil S, Bauteil T Die Sanierung erfolgt abschnittsweise in drei Bauabschnitten. BA 1: Gebäudeteil A, B, L BA 2: Gebäudeteile P, R, O BA 3: Gebäudeteil C, L, M, F und Pausenhöfe Die jeweiligen Bauabschnitte sind zeitlich wie folgt geplant: BA 1: 06.10.2025 - 12.2026 BA 2: 01.2026 - 12.2027 02.11.2026 - 02.2028 (P Schwimmhalle) BA 3: 01.2027 - 10.2028 Dachraum als Sonderabschnitt: Die Arbeiten erfolgen für diesen Bauabschnitt parallel zu den anderen Bauabschnitten in Absprache mit Bauleitung und AG.

title: CA18575 - RFQ 2026/42 - Conservation Engineer for St Paul's Church The Crag Cemetery Rostrevor
description: Newry, Mourne & Down District Council looking for a Conservation Engineer who shall undertake a structural assessment of St Paul's Church and its environs and prepare a phased, costed conservation strategy addressing short-, medium- and long-term actions. St Paul's Church (ruins) is located within Crag Cemetery in the Rostrevor Conservation Area. The cemetery is accessed via a lane off Mary Street/The Square and is bounded by St Bronagh's GAA Clubrooms to the west, with residential development to the south and east. While the church is neither listed in its own right nor a scheduled monument, it is considered curtilage listed due to its proximity to a Grade B listed memorial (HB16/06/050). The church ruins are in a deteriorated and unstable condition, which has led to the closure of the graveyard on health and safety grounds. This has significant implications for public access, heritage value and community use. A structural appraisal was undertaken in 2019, with further recommendations issued in 2021. Although initial actions were progressed, the project subsequently stalled due to COVID-19 disruption and changes in personnel. The condition of the structure has since worsened, and the site remains closed. To access this competition: Registered: Login to https://suppliers.multiquote.com and view the opportunity CA18575. Not registered: Visit https://suppliers.multiquote.com then register and quote CA18575 as the reason for registration. Any queries please contact MultiQuote on 020 3920 8054.

The contractor will deliver expertise in programme management, monitoring, evaluation, and stakeholder coordination. Services include analytical support, drafting reports and studies, organising workshops and events, and maintaining knowledge-sharing platforms. The contractor will also support project selection, assessment processes, and capacity-building activities for programme beneficiaries. All services must align with EU regulations and the strategic objectives of the programmes. The nature of the work is demand-driven, varying according to programme priorities and emerging needs. Quantities of services will be defined through specific assignments, including expert days, operational support, and deliverables. The overall aim is to ensure efficient, transparent, and high-quality programme implementation. The contract contributes to policy learning, knowledge exchange, and enhanced cooperation among participating regions. By providing flexible and specialised support, the contractor enables the programmes to meet their objectives. (2026CE160AT059)

description: Sources Sought Notice THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. THE GOVERNMENT WILL NOT PAY NOR REIMBURSE ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH RESPONDING TO THIS REQUEST. THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. The Department of Veterans Affairs is seeking a qualified Architect-Engineering (AE) firm to provide Schematics, Design Development, Construction Documents, Technical Specifications, Construction Period Services, Site Visits, Cost Estimates, As-Built Documentation, and all other related information for Project 58A5-27-503 Project Design Replace Flat Roof at the Canandaigua VA Medical Center, 400 Fort Hill Avenue, Canandaigua, NY 14424. this project is to develop a conditions-report and design documents for replacing the existing flat roofs on buildings 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 36, 37, 118, and various connecting tunnels. The conditions report shall be prepared after a thorough investigation of the existing conditions with estimated costs and improvements. The following design will include all selected repairs and improvements from the conditions report that fit within VA construction budget. As part of the report and design effort, the existing conditions shall be tested and verified, including evaluation of the drainage, materiality, masonry, fall protection, equipment, ACM, insulation, and structural integrity. New work may include redesign / reconstruction of support structures, drainage, roof type change, and parapet wall restoration to ensure water intrusion and legacy issues are mitigated. In addition to repairs and modifications, all interior drainage piping shall be replaced minimum 10 from roof drain unless, otherwise discussed with VA for convenience or practical reasons or as needed due to conditions of ease or degradation. This requirement is being procured in accordance with the Brooks Act as implemented in FAR Subpart 36.6. Applicable NAICS code is 541330 and small business size standard of $25.5 Million. Magnitude of Construction is between $500,000 and $1,000,000. This is a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Set Aside. The anticipated award date of the proposed A-E Contract is on or before December 30, 2026. Potential contractors must be registered in SAM (www.sam.gov ) and are visible/verified/certified as SDVOSB in Dynamic Small Business Search (https://dsbs.sba.gov/search/dsp_dsbs.cfm) at time of submission of their qualifications in order to be considered for an award. In order to assure compliance with VAAR clauses, 852.219-75 VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction (NOV 2022) and 852.219-73 VA Notice to Total Set-Aside for Verified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (NOV 2022), all firms submitting a SF 330 for this notice are required to indicate what percentage of the cost of contract performance will be expended on the concerns employees and in which discipline(s) and percentage of cost of contract performance to be expended (and in what disciplines) by any other consultant/subcontractor or otherwise used small or large business entity(s). Any consultant/subcontractor or otherwise business entity(s) used must be identified by name, office location and size/type of business (i.e., SDVOSB, VOSB, 8(a), small, large, etc.). Failure to provide this information will deem the firm s SF 330 submittal as non-responsive and preclude further evaluation All A/E firms are advised that in accordance with VAAR 836.606-71 the total cost of the production and delivery of designs, plans, drawings and specifications shall not exceed six (6) percent of the estimate cost of construction. Other A-E fees are not included in the six (6) percent. Additionally, FAR Clause 52.236-22 (c) - Design Within Funding Limitation, will be applicable to this procurement action. SCOPE OF SERVICE REQUIRED Project no. 528A5-27-503: A/E Design Replace Flat Roof LOCATION Canandaigua VAMC, 400 Fort Hill Avenue Canandaigua, NY 14424 COST RANGE Magnitude of Construction is between $500,000.00 and $1,000,000.00 Estimated Construction Cost Range: $5,000,000. TYPE OF CONTRACT CONTEMPLATED The Department of Veterans Affairs is contemplating awarding a firm fixed price contract. DESIGN COMPLETION PERIOD: The Department of Veterans Affairs requires design and contract support services. The A/E shall deliver 100% bid documents in 255 calendar days from the Notice to Proceed (NTP). SELECTION CRITERIA DESCRIPTIONS The submitted SF-330s will be evaluated on the following criteria: This acquisition will be in accordance with FAR Part 36.602-1 and VAAR Part 836.602-1. The following evaluation criteria will be used to evaluate SF-330 technical proposals: The A/E must demonstrate its qualifications with respect to the published evaluation criteria for all services. Evaluation Criteria is of equal importance with an exception of criterion 1 and 7 which shall carry an additional weight multiplier of 1.5. Each criterion shall be rated out of a score of 1 to 10. Total possible score is 80. Specific evaluation criteria include: 1.Specialized experience and technical competence in the type of work required, including, roof replacements, structural repairs, drainage, temporary systems and investigative services. 2. Professional Qualifications necessary for performance of site surveys such as the one described within the SOW including qualified personnel and approach to this scope. 3. Capacity to accomplish the work in the required time. 4. Past Performance on contracts with Government agencies and private industry in terms of cost control, quality of work and compliance with performance schedules. 5. Specific experience and qualifications of personnel proposed for assignment to the project and their record of working together as a team. 6. Location in the general geographical area of the project and knowledge of the locality of the project; provided, that application of this criterion leaves an appropriate number of qualified firms, given the nature and size of the project. 7. Specific examples of survey documents as described in the scope of work and approach to preparation of the documents as requested by the VA. 8. Record of significant claims against the firm because of improper or incomplete architectural and engineering services. Criterion 1 - Specialized experience and technical competence in the type of work required, including, roof replacements, structural repairs, drainage, temporary systems and investigative services. Offerors will be evaluated on specialized experience and technical competence in the performance of services similar to those anticipated under this contract with regard to: Experience with roofing systems. Experience with design of building drainage systems. Experience with specialized HVAC and electrical design for healthcare facilities. Experience in providing post construction award services (shop drawing review, as-built drawing and Quality Assurance Plan (QAP) preparation, construction inspection services, and Operating and Maintenance Manuals). Experience with government designs and construction. Experience with historic buildings, preservation, and alterations. Submission requirements: Provide a detailed write-up of how the firm has accomplished the requirement. In addition, provide up to five (5) projects completed or substantially completed within the past five (5) years that best illustrate specialized experience of the proposed team in the areas outlined above. Example projects shall note project s square footage. All projects provided in the SF-330 must be completed by the office/branch/regional office/individual team member actually proposed to manage and/or perform work under this contract. title: RFI Comprehensive Medical Review & Audit Support
description: This Request for Information (RFI) is issued in accordance with FAR Part 10 to conduct market research. The Government's purpose is planning only; this notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP)/Request for Quotation (RFQ) nor a promise to issue one in the future. The Government will not pay any costs for responding, and any submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future procurement. The Government is not seeking proposals or quotes at this time. Scope of Interest / Functional Areas: The Government is assessing the market�s capability to provide comprehensive support under the following disciplines: a. Audits for Medicare Parts A, B, D, and Medicaid medical record review and consultative services b. Audits for Medicare Part C medical record review and consultative services c. Evaluations and Inspections medical record review and consultative services d. Expert consultant and witness services in support of the Office of Investigations and/or Office of Counsel to the Inspector General A draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) is provided for industry feedback; requirements may change prior to any future solicitation. Requested Information (do not submit proposals or quotes): Please provide high level, non price specific information addressing the elements below. Do not include proprietary pricing, line item estimates, or any proposal/quote content. Section 1: Corporate Capability & Experience a. PWS Alignment: Demonstrate your organization's core capability to fulfill the functional areas outlined in the draft PWS. b. Medical Review Experience: Outline your firm's high-level experience in conducting large-volume medical claims reviews for audits and evaluations and inspections; and support services for medical expert consultants and witnesses specifically across the following five domains (as referenced in the attached PWS): 1. Audit Medicare Parts A/B/D and Medicaid 2. Audit Medicare Part C 3. Evaluations and Inspections 4. Office of Investigations 5. Office of Counsel to the Inspector General c. Geographic Reach: Describe your prior experience managing and executing nationwide or multi-jurisdictional medical claim reviews. d. Capacity & Scalability: State your organization's maximum monthly claim review capacity, including your approach to scaling operations between normal workloads and surge conditions. e Teaming & Subcontracting: Identify potential subcontracting partners or specialized vendors you would anticipate utilizing, including an estimated percentage breakdown of work performed by the prime contractor versus subcontractors. Section 2: High-Level Technical Approach & Operations a. High-Level Technical Methodology: Describe your conceptual approach to fulfilling the core tasks in PWS. Please limit this narrative to no more than 5 pages total, organized by the 5 PWS sections. Focus on your overarching claims review methodology, general sampling plan frameworks, documentation standards, and typical project timelines rather than a granular, step-by-step solution. b. Quality & Accuracy Frameworks: Outline your corporate quality assurance processes, internal review protocols, and standard strategies used to reduce error rates and ensure consistency across large volumes. b. Staffing & Key Qualifications: Provide a conceptual staffing structure or organizational chart. Identify the typical roles, credentials (e.g., MD, RN, CPC), and qualifications of the key personnel required to successfully support a PWS of this nature. Please identify whether these staff will need to be hired or if they are current employees/contractors. Also, indicate staffing availability for physicians with specialties (i.e. hospice, vascular surgeon, nephrologist, physical medicine and rehabilitation or physiatrists). c. Risk & Mitigation: Identify the primary technical or operational challenges anticipated with a medical review scope of this size and outline your high-level mitigation strategies. Section 3: Past Performance & Market Pricing a. Relevant Past Performance: Provide up to three examples of similar Federal medical review contracts performed within the last five years. Also, provide up to three examples of similar Federal support services for medical expert consultants and witnesses within the last five years. b. Performance Outcomes: Summarize the high-level outcomes of those past contracts, focusing on standard metrics such as timeliness, accuracy rates (including rate at which findings were overturned during the appeals process), and a history of successful audit findings. c. Cost Drivers & Efficiencies: Provide a general overview of your commercial pricing structure and the primary cost drivers (e.g., specific labor categories, specialized technology/AI tools, administrative overhead). Highlight any built-in efficiencies or innovative workflows in your approach that typically yield cost savings for the government. Section 4: Industry Feedback & PWS Refinement a. Clarity & Feasibility Review: Identify any requirements, metrics, or tasks within the draft PWS that appear ambiguous, overly restrictive, or technologically infeasible based on current commercial market capabilities. b. Recommendations for Improvement: Suggest specific enhancements, industry standard metrics, or structural changes to the PWS that would improve the clarity, feasibility, and competitiveness of the final solicitation. Submission Instructions: Email responses by November 13, 2026, 12:00 PM Eastern Time to the Points of Contact below. Mark proprietary information clearly; the Government may use non proprietary information to refine its acquisition approach. Points of Contact: a. Contracting Officer: Shavonda Jamison � Shavonda_Jamison@ibc.doi.gov b. Contracting Specialist: Dorothy Royster � Dorothy_Royster@ibc.doi.gov Attachments: a. Draft PWS (for market research and feedback only; subject to change). Disclaimer: This RFI is for market research; it does not commit the Government to any acquisition. The Government will not reimburse costs for responding. Not responding does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. No proposals or quotes will be accepted in response to this notice.

title: Commercial Kennels/Boarding Military Working Dogs
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The Marine Corps Installations National Capital Region � Regional Contracting Office (MCINCR-RCO), located at Marine Corps Base Quantico, VA, is conducting market research on behalf of the Provost Marshall Office Quantico VA. The purpose is to identify vendors capable of providing kennels and boarding for an estimated amount of 10 to 20 Military Working Dogs for an estimated time of 24 to 48 months. CONTRACTING OFFICE ADDRESS: Marine Corps Installations � National Capital Region, Regional Contracting Office (MCINCR RCO), located on Marine Corps Base, 2010 Henderson Road, Quantico, VA. INTRODUCTION: This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for market research and planning purposes. It provides industry an opportunity to ask questions and offer suggestions regarding the draft technical specifications outlined in the Capabilities Statement below. DISCLAIMER: THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMAITON IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ). IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION: Estimated quantity: 10 to 20 Military working dogs Time: 24 to 48 months Requested starting date: 1 December 2025 or sooner or as soon as possible The minimum run size of 8x8 Facilities are required to be within the immediate geographic area of Quantico, Virginia. 24/7 access by us, and no access by anyone else to include kennel employees Break yard access dedicated to our MWDS Can not be housed or share common areas with other pets At least one Quarantine kennel (could be an option, as it would only be needed if a new dog arrives, or a dog gets ill) The following are only needed if we are completely barred from utilizing the current facility for non-housing (i.e., we can still use the works spaces and utilities and even bath the dogs, just can�t put them in the runs�) Storage for food and Medication Bathing station for MWD�s Feed Prep area with sink to clean food bowls and water bowls Washer and Dryer to clean equipment (towels, rags, sleeves) INDUSTRY FEEDBACK: This is a REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY to obtain industry�s feedback on the anticipated technical specifications, potential cost and performance risks, as well as any other related considerations for the required supplies/services. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely to gather industry feedback regarding the anticipated technical specifications, cost and performance risks, and other relevant considerations associated with the required supplies and/or services. Please provide input on the following: Capability: Can your organization deliver all products and services outlined in the Requirement Description? Barriers to Competition: Are there any conditions, certifications, or proprietary constraints that could limit fair competition? Proposal Interest: Are you likely to submit a proposal for this requirement? Please explain your reasoning. Commercial Availability: Is this product/service commonly available in the commercial market? Pricing Structure: Can this requirement be fulfilled under a Firm Fixed Price contract? Competition Influencers: Are there any specific conditions, requirements, or limitations that could affect open and fair competition? Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) pricing gives the draft requirements. If unable to generate estimates at this stage, specify what additional information would be needed. Pricing should reflect all costs associated with course development and delivery, including travel expenses, if applicable. Please note that the ROM pricing is non-binding and shall not be construed as a formal pricing proposal. NAICS Classification: What North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code(s) best align with this requirement? SUBMISSION DETAILS: Submissions shall reference RFI No. �M00264-26-RFI-001A �Boarding for Military Working Dogs� in the subject line. Interested vendors who wish to respond to this RFI should send responses no later than 12:00PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 13 November 2025, via email to the following email addresses: hal.d.jones@usmc.mil and sharon.palustre@usmc.mil. Request responses shall be provided in no more than 4 pages. Questions and comments regarding this requirement will be accepted, reviewed and answered if the Government determines responses are warranted. The Government will not consider any vendor email that is incomplete or is not addressing this RFI questions. The Government reserves the right to determine if a response addresses this RFI, is not complete, and/or to not review a response without any further communication with the vendor supplying the information. Submissions must include: 1) Responses to the �Industry Feedback� section of this RFI. 2) Business name and address. 3) Name of company representative, their business title and insurance. 4) Type of Business. 5) Cage Code and UEI; and 6) Contract vehicles that would be available to the Government for the procurement of the service, to include General Service Administration (GSA), Federal Supply Schedules (FSS), or any other Government Agency contract vehicle. (This information is for market research only and does not preclude your company from responding to this notice.) 8) Delivery Information Estimate lead time. title: Quality Assurance Services - Civil Works, Interagency and International Services (IIS), and Military Construction Projects in Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Caribbean District issues this Request for Proposals (RFP) to award an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) for Quality Assurance Services across Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. This procurement follows the presolicitation notice previously synopsized under solicitation number W51DQV26RA007. The contractor shall provide comprehensive quality assurance oversight supporting Civil Works, International and Interagency Services (IIS), and Military Construction (MILCON) projects, including navigation, flood risk management, coastal protection, environmental restoration, water resources, and military or federal installations. Services encompass monitoring contractor compliance with plans and specifications, reviewing engineering submittals and technical reports, conducting on-site field inspections of dams, levees, berms, cutoff walls, pump stations, flood control gates, and electrical systems, and performing certified sampling and laboratory testing of soil, concrete, and water. Contract personnel shall also perform daily safety monitoring and prepare daily quality assurance inspection reports. This action is a total small business set-aside under NAICS code 541990 (All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services) with an applicable small business size standard of $19.5 million. The contract ordering period comprises a one-year base period, four 12-month option periods, and one six-month option period, not to exceed a total duration of five years and six months, with a maximum program capacity of $35 million across the contract life.

title: E-Waste Collection Events
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance LLC (BEA), the Management and Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from qualified recyclers capable of organizing residential electronic waste (e-waste) collection events in states without e-waste recycling regulation (i.e., nonregulated states) to support INL�s research and operational mission. This service is essential for raising awareness, increasing collection volumes and verifying whether successful collection methods from a regulated state can be applied to a nonregulated state with comparable results. Eligible states for this work include Alabama, Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Idaho (except eastern and southeastern region), Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Dakota, Ohio, South Dakota, Tennessee and Wyoming. BACKGROUND BEA is the Management and Operating Contractor for the DOE located at INL. INL is a DOE national laboratory dedicated to nuclear energy, national security and advanced energy innovation. A BEA research team has the lead role on the DOE project titled, �Comparing Strategies to Collect Battery-Containing Devices in States with and without Electronics Recycling Laws.� The proposed service will operate to support this project through Sept. 30, 2027. In the first two years of this project, project teams organized collection events in New York and Idaho. New York is as urban area with established e-waste regulations, and Idaho is a rural area without such requirements. By applying successful collection methods from New York to southeastern Idaho, we observed similar success across 20 e-waste collection events. To further validate these results, we are seeking opportunities to apply our methods in other nonregulated states by organizing six to nine e-waste collection events. SCOPE OF WORK Responding organizations must be capable of delivering the following services: Provide existing status; compile data from existing residential collection activities related to seasonal trends, locations and e-waste types. Organize collection events at new locations in nonregulated states, with each participating organization conducting at least two to three collection events before September 2027. Arrange advertisements on multiple channels to broadcast new collection events and raise awareness about battery-containing e-waste recycling. Provide collection event data including number of participants and quantities of collected e-waste by type PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested vendors should submit an EOI that includes the following: Organization information: Organization name, address, organization type, scope of operations, number of employees and primary point of contact. Existing e-waste collection access: Describe existing e-waste collection events, permanent drop-off locations or other collection options available in the proposed service area. Program interest and expected outcomes: Explain why your organization wants to participate in this project and what outcomes you expect to achieve. Service area and target participants: Identify the cities, counties, or communities that will be served by the proposed e-waste collection activities. Community need: Describe the primary e-waste management challenges or unmet needs in the proposed service area. Collection plan: Describe the proposed e-waste collection activities for the program year (by Sept. 1, 2027). Provide the anticipated number of collection events and proposed cities, counties, or collection locations. Provide communication strategies (i.e. social media, mail, news, flyers, etc.) to raise awareness and promote collection events. Downstream e-waste management: Identify who will transport, receive, recycle, process, or otherwise manage the collected e-waste. Recycler/processor qualifications: Identify relevant certifications or qualifications of the entities handling collected e-waste, such as R2, e-Stewards, or other applicable certifications. title: Vacuum Turbo Pumps
description: This is a request for information (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS. This request is not a solicitation (Request for Proposal or Request for Quotations) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this request for information is in support of market research being conducted by the Air Force Metrology Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) to identify potential sources and gather information on current capabilities within the market. This synopsis is for planning purposes only and is NOT to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited hereunder. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party's expense. The level of security clearance and amount of foreign participation in this requirement has not been determined. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked PROPRIETARY will be handled accordingly. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. Proprietary information or trade secrets should be clearly identified. If, after reviewing these documents, you desire to participate in the market research, you should provide documentation that supports your company's capability in meeting these requirements. Failure to provide documentation may result in the government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a particular area, please provide details explaining how you would overcome the lack of experience/capabilities in order to perform that portion of the requirement (i.e., teaming, subcontracting, etc.) Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint ventures or teaming arrangements are encouraged. Currently there are no funds available for this acquisition. The Air Force Metrology and Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing Turbomolecular Pumping Stations. The Turbomolecular Pumping Station (TMPS) will replace the Agilent Technologies/Varian TPS-compact TV301 (Model: 969-8221M003), which contains the following components: TV301 turbomolecular pump, integrated controller, variable leak valve and dry scroll backing pump. The manufacturer (Agilent/Varian) has discontinued this item and ceased its support of the key components. This acquisition will aid AFMETCAL in maintaining support for a multitude of different high-vacuum and vacuum metrology calibration equipment across the Air Force. The new standard would support high-vacuum chambers, vacuum sensors, transducers, and other similar high-vacuum TMDE. The TMPS shall evacuate vacuum TMDE up to high-vacuum levels in absolute mode. Responses will assist AFMETCAL in determining the availability of qualified sources and the appropriate acquisition strategy. Interested vendors should submit a brief capability statement including company information (DUNS, CAGE, business size), relevant experience, and rough order of magnitude pricing. The NAICS code assigned to this acquisition is 334515 with a size standard of 750 employees. The total estimated quantity of 86 units over 5 years. Reconditioned, remanufactured, or used material is not acceptable for this item. Offerors responding to this sources sought market research notice must: (1) state whether you are a small or large business, if you are the manufacturer or provide the name of the manufacturer and size info of product you would be offering and the socioeconomic status and indicate small disadvantaged or woman-owned business, veteran owned, service disabled veteran owned, 8(a) historically black college or university or minority institution (HBCU/MI), or a historically underutilized business zone (HUBZone) (2) provide sales history including recent sales to commercial companies (3) advise if your product is a commercial item or if it will be modified; if not commercial at this time, will you be offering this item to the general public in the future. (4) advise if you have the item on a GSA schedule or other Government contract include front page of schedule and the page showing the part is on award (5) provide information concerning the technical capabilities of the product you are interested in offering, including commercial literature/brochures and warranty. Describe any awards you have been involved in that are the same as or similar to what is described in this RFI. Include any other pertinent information which would enable the government to assess your firm�s capabilities (6) advise if you accept the Government purchase card (7) Provide Point of Contact including: company/ institute name, address, phone number and email address (8) provide assigned Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code (9) Verify if your company/institute is listed in the System for Award Management (SAM) (10) State if your company is domestically or foreign owned (if foreign owned, please indicate the country of ownership) (11) Advise how much time you would need to submit a technical proposal if a solicitation is issued (12) provide an estimated price for one each, an estimated price for the total quantity and provide any price quantity discounts based on the total estimated quantity (13) include estimated delivery time for shipment. Ensure only .pdf, .doc or .xls documents are attached to your email. Submit all responses to the listed point of contact. If an email response is not possible, submit by FAX to 937-713-5841 or mail to 813 Irving-wick Dr W., Horton Building, Heath OH 43056-1199. Reference 27M-083A-VA in all correspondence. Responses are due by 11/13/2026 at 2:00pm ET or 1400 hours; however, early responses are encouraged. Phase I: The Government will evaluate written proposals under the following factors in accordance with Section M of the solicitation: Factor I � Mission Effectiveness (Non-Price) Factor II � Production and Management (Non-Price) Factor III � Price Following the Phase I evaluation and best-value tradeoff, the Government may select up to four (4) Offerors for award of IDIQ contracts. Each Phase I awardee will receive an initial Delivery Order satisfying the contract minimum guarantee for the construction and delivery of one (1) demonstrator boat and trailer for participation in Phase II. Phase II: Phase I awardees will participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration lasting up to 90 calendar days. Phase II will evaluate: Factor IV � In-Water Demonstration (Non-Price) Factor III � Price (carries forward from Phase I, not a new price evaluation) Phase II is an independent evaluation. Phase I evaluation results, other than carrying the price evaluation forward, will not influence the Phase II evaluation. The Technical Evaluation Team (TET) will use the In-Water Demonstration Report and documented personal observations during the In-Water Demonstration to conduct a comparative evaluation of how each demonstrator boat performed in comparison to the other demonstrator boats. The TET will document the specific technical advantages and disadvantages identified through the comparative evaluation under Factor IV. Following completion of Phase II, the Government will conduct a final best-value tradeoff evaluation and select one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive all subsequent production Delivery Orders for the remaining RB-S III boats. Price evaluations will remain unchanged from Phase I; no price revisions or updates will be permitted in Phase II. title: Solicitation: Construct Combat Rescue Helicopter Flight Simulator Facility at Moffett ANGB
description: The Contractor shall provide non-personal services, to include all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the construction of a Combat Rescue Helicopter (CRH) Operational Flight Trainer (OFT) simulator facility at Moffett Air National Guard Base (ANGB), Mountain View, California. This project will provide an approximately 8,202 gross square foot building consisting of a multi-story, high bay area to house the CRH-OFT simulator, with a single-story area containing CRH mission planning, briefing and debriefing rooms, administrative areas for training and support staff, OFT maintenance and parts storage rooms, secure and non-secure telecommunication rooms, latrine facilities and mechanical, electrical and utility support rooms utilizing conventional design and construction. The building will be of permanent construction with electrical, mechanical, HVAC, plumbing, wet sprinkler fire suppression, fire detection, access control, direct digital control, and utility management. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Air space and insulation to be located inside the cavity wall to meet Energy Code requirements. The primary roofing materials will be standing seam metal roofing to match other installation facilities and the perimeter sloped roof design will include a prefinished standing seam metal roof panel system over rigid insulation. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Main entrance doors will be a pair of anodized aluminum storefront entrance doors with insulating glass including a sidelight. The Mechanical, Electrical, Sim Bay and secondary egress doors will be painted, insulated hollow metal door and frames with controlled access. Antiterrorism/Force Protection elements are incorporated. Supporting facilities include landscaping, utilities, pavements, storm drainage, sanitary sewer, site improvements, communications support, cybersecurity control systems, and tempest security.

title: Solicitation: Construct Combat Rescue Helicopter Flight Simulator Facility at Moffett ANGB
description: The Contractor shall provide non-personal services, to include all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the construction of a Combat Rescue Helicopter (CRH) Operational Flight Trainer (OFT) simulator facility at Moffett Air National Guard Base (ANGB), Mountain View, California. This project will provide an approximately 8,202 gross square foot building consisting of a multi-story, high bay area to house the CRH-OFT simulator, with a single-story area containing CRH mission planning, briefing and debriefing rooms, administrative areas for training and support staff, OFT maintenance and parts storage rooms, secure and non-secure telecommunication rooms, latrine facilities and mechanical, electrical and utility support rooms utilizing conventional design and construction. The building will be of permanent construction with electrical, mechanical, HVAC, plumbing, wet sprinkler fire suppression, fire detection, access control, direct digital control, and utility management. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Air space and insulation to be located inside the cavity wall to meet Energy Code requirements. The primary roofing materials will be standing seam metal roofing to match other installation facilities and the perimeter sloped roof design will include a prefinished standing seam metal roof panel system over rigid insulation. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Main entrance doors will be a pair of anodized aluminum storefront entrance doors with insulating glass including a sidelight. The Mechanical, Electrical, Sim Bay and secondary egress doors will be painted, insulated hollow metal door and frames with controlled access. Antiterrorism/Force Protection elements are incorporated. Supporting facilities include landscaping, utilities, pavements, storm drainage, sanitary sewer, site improvements, communications support, cybersecurity control systems, and tempest security.

title: Domestic Aviation Design Industry Day
description: Domestic Aviation Design Industry Day Important Dates: Industry Day Registration Deadline -- 3:00 PM EDT on Friday, November 13, 2026 Industry Day -- 9:00 AM EDT on Tuesday, November 17, 2026 1. Introduction For over 10 years, TSA has held regular events to engage with external aviation security stakeholders, including airports, airport designers, airlines, equipment vendors, industry groups, and other domestic and international industry stakeholders in support of TSA�s mission. TSA has capitalized on these events to: Promote TSA�s checkpoint system of systems designs and standards; Encourage collaboration within the aviation security community; Share best practices from a variety of operating environments, facility sizes, and capabilities; Learn about the latest security technology advances and industry innovations; and Engage with stakeholders early in the design process to allow TSA to influence designs and support public-private partnerships. 2. Purpose The Domestic Aviation Design Industry Day is a forum for engaging the communities implementing aviation security in a collaborative environment, consistent with TSA strategic priorities to Improve Security, Safeguard the Transportation System, and Accelerate Action. 3. Event Description: Date: Tuesday, November 17, 2026 9:00 AM EDT Location: Virtual (Microsoft Teams) TSA intends to cover updates related to the Checkpoint Requirements and Planning Guide (CRPG), the Planning Guidelines and Design Standards (PGDS), and Donations. 4. Agenda (See attached) 5. Required Criteria for Attendance: Participation in the Industry Day is limited to representatives from the following organization categories: a. Transportation security equipment manufacturers; b. Checkpoint designers; c. Checked baggage inspection system designers; d. Systems integrators; e. Airlines; f. Airport authorities; g. Aviation industry associations; and h. Federal, state, and local government entities. To be considered for attendance, each responding organization must submit a one- to three-sentence summary describing its relevant experience and any other pertinent information demonstrating that it qualifies under one or more of the categories listed above. 6. Registration: The following information must be submitted (with the information in Section 5) to CheckpointRequirements@tsa.dhs.gov no later than 3:00 PM EDT on Friday, November 13, 2026 in the format below: Attendee First Name, Attendee Last Name, Agency/Company/Airport, Attendee Email Address/ Category/Categories per Section 5, one- to three-sentence summary describing Relevant Experience and any other pertinent information demonstrating qualification under the referenced category. TSA will send a confirmation email with Industry Day details to those who are accepted by TSA to attend this Industry Day. Acceptance from TSA for attendance at this event is subject to TSA�s sole review and discretion. Satisfaction of the Required Criteria for Attendance, registration for the event, and acceptance by TSA is required. 7. Post Industry Day Any questions or comments after the industry day should be directed to CheckpointRequirements@tsa.dhs.gov. **Disclaimer- This Industry Day is being held for market research and industry engagement. Attendance is voluntary and the Government will not pay for attendance or travel. Organizations responding to this announcement are solely responsible for all expenses associated with their responses to this announcement and with attendance.**

title: Automated Celestial Navigation System (ACNS) Production
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS PUBLISHED FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THE GOVERNMENT IS NOT SEEKING OR ACCEPTING UNSOLICITED PROPOSALS. This notice is a Request for Information (RFI) as defined in FAR 15.101(c). The Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) is conducting market research for the Automated Celestial Navigation System (ACNS). ACNS helps to determine vessel position based on optical sighting of celestial objects including stars and resident space objects (RSOs) such as satellites and space debris. Ship�s position derived from ACNS shall be used to improve the resilience of the surface ship Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) system of systems suite by providing an Alternative Position Source (APS) to support Assured PNT. U.S. Navy and commercial enterprises leverage a variety of navigation solutions that allow vessels to safely navigate with and without GPS. title: CPE CBRND Seeking Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) of Silicon Dioxide (SiO2) on Aluminum Flakes for Screening Obscuration Module - Multispectral (SOM-M)
description: 1.0 Disclaimer This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the U.S. Government (USG) to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Furthermore, the USG will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this RFI. Responders are advised that the USG will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. The information gathered by this RFI will be shared with relevant interested USG parties to help inform future development and procurement efforts. 2.0 Background The Joint Product Manager for CBRN Layered Effects is responsible for enabling and enhancing the survivability of our Joint Warfighters so they can fight and win across all domains in a CBRN-contested environment. As the acquisition leader in mobile analytics, our portfolio provides transformative solutions � including advanced reconnaissance systems, sensors, and mobile analytical laboratories � that ensure our military is safeguarded against chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats. To support this mission, the USG is pursuing the Screening Obscuration Module - Multispectral (SOM-M) program, which is envisioned as a modular, man-portable, ground-emplaced obscuration and screening system designed to produce a multispectral obscurant cloud for both mounted and dismounted use. In support of the SOM-M program, the USG is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify alternative, cost-effective commercial manufacturing options for critical, novel bispectral obscurant material. The technical requirements for this capability are detailed in Section 4.0 of this document. 3.0 Purpose The purpose of this RFI is to survey industry capabilities and identify alternative commercial manufacturing options for a novel bispectral obscurant material. Specifically, the USG seeks to identify manufacturers capable of performing high-volume Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) of Silicon Dioxide (SiO2) onto Aluminum Flakes at a commercial scale, and to assess industry readiness to support a potential Army-funded manufacturing maturation project aimed at reducing sustainment costs. 4.0 Technical Requirements Interested parties must demonstrate capabilities or conceptual pathways to meet the following production and material requirements: Base Material & Size: Aluminum Flake sized at 2 � 4 microns. Coating Process & Material: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) of Silicon Dioxide (SiO2) onto the aluminum flakes. Target Production Volume: Scalable to large commercial quantities, ranging from hundreds of pounds (lbs) to tons. Cost Efficiency: Proposed alternative manufacturing options must significantly reduce current manufacturing protocol costs to ensure long-term sustainment capability for the military services. 5.0 Requested Information Interested parties are requested to respond to this RFI providing a white paper including technical insights on the manufacturing feasibility, cost-effectiveness, and scalability of the proposed Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) process. Ideal responses will include the following elements: Manufacturing/Production Approach: A comprehensive overview of the proposed methodology to achieve the PVD coating of Silicon Dioxide (SiO2) on Aluminum Flakes (2 � 4 microns). This should include details on the facility scale, equipment, and proposed lead times based on the scale of material produced. Cost Projections & Scale: Estimated cost profiles and projected cost-reduction curves when scaling production from hundreds of pounds to tons, demonstrating how the approach achieves a sustainable cost profile for long term acquisition. Maturity, Capacity, & Risks: An assessment of current facility readiness, current and potential production capacity, and identified technical and manufacturing challenges or risk factors associated with scaling this specific PVD coating process. Company Information & Past Performance: A brief summary of relevant company experience, facility capabilities, or prior similar material coating efforts. 6.0 Submission Requirements All submissions must be electronic and adhere to the following formatting and content rules: Page Limit: All responses shall be no longer than five (5) pages. Formatting: Standard 8.5 x 11-inch pages, with font size no smaller than 10-point. Company Information: Include official company name, address, telephone number, website, and business type (large/small business classification), CAGE Code. Point of Contact: Provide the name, title, telephone number, and email address of the authorized company representative. 7.0 Submission Guidance Submission Deadline: Responses are requested no later than 5 PM EST Friday, 13 November 2026. Submissions and/or questions should be emailed directly to the following point of contact: Emily McGill, Contract Specialist, emily.c.mcgill.civ@army.mil Samantha Degele, Contracting Officer, samantha.l.degele.civ@army.mil

title: École Kleinfeld-Druckiareal, Mels - Concours de projets en une étape avec présélection
description:
Dans la commune de Mels, dans le Sarganserland, l’évolution des exigences pédagogiques ainsi que l’augmentation des effectifs scolaires entraînent un besoin accru en locaux scolaires. Compte tenu de la forte hausse du nombre d’élèves au degré primaire et afin de prévenir les éventuelles insuffisances de capacités, tant actuelles que futures, le site scolaire de Kleinfeld-Druckiareal doit être agrandi.À terme, le site devra accueillir les classes de la 1re à la 4e année primaire, divers espaces d’apprentissage, espaces sociaux, locaux thérapeutiques et espaces dédiés aux activités créatives, un jardin d’enfants ainsi que la structure d’accueil Melsolino. Le programme comprendra également une salle de sport triple, une salle de lutte suisse ainsi qu’un parking souterrain public d’environ 50 places.

 

Afin d’obtenir des propositions de solutions pour la conception et la réalisation de l’extension du complexe scolaire de Kleinfeld-Druckiareal, la commune de Mels organise un concours de projets en une étape, selon une procédure sélective. Le concours s’adresse à des équipes pluridisciplinaires composées de spécialistes des domaines de l’architecture, de l’ingénierie civile (structures) et de l’architecture paysagère.

 

La procédure fera l’objet d’un appel à candidatures publié sur la plateforme de publication officielle www.simap.ch. Toutes les personnes et équipes intéressées remplissant les conditions de participation pourront déposer un dossier de candidature dans le cadre de la phase de présélection (préqualification).

Sur la base des critères d’aptitude, 12 à 15 équipes seront sélectionnées pour participer au concours de projets. Parmi celles-ci, un maximum de deux jeunes bureaux d’architecture pourra être admis au sein de la discipline architecture

title: Prestations d’exploitation IT externalisées
description:
Monthey Energies souhaite confier à un prestataire spécialisé la mise en place et l’exploitation de son environnement informatique cible. Ces prestations devront être transférées dans un environnement propre à Monthey Energies, avec une sortie de l’infrastructure VDI actuelle.


Le marché comprend les prestations suivantes :

  • la préparation et la réalisation de la migration
  • l’hébergement en Suisse et l’exploitation technique des applications Care Office, Infra Data et UNIMOD, de leurs bases de données et des composants nécessaires à leur fonctionnement ;
  • la fourniture des licences, la création, la sécurisation, la migration et l’administration d’un tenant Microsoft 365 dédié, les services Microsoft 365 restant hébergés par Microsoft selon les exigences du cahier des charges technique ;
  • les services IT managés, comprenant le support aux utilisateurs, la gestion des identités et des accès, des postes de travail, des terminaux mobiles, du réseau et de la sécurité, ainsi que la coordination avec les fournisseurs tiers ;
  • la fourniture et la gestion du matériel et des accessoires,
  • la sauvegarde et la restauration des données et des environnements couverts, y compris les données Microsoft 365, ainsi que les dispositifs de continuité et de reprise.
  • la documentation, le transfert de connaissances et la réversibilité des prestations.


L’hébergement et l’exploitation applicative des solutions maintenues par des tiers identifiées dans le cahier des charges technique, sont exclus du marché. Le titulaire assurera néanmoins les conditions techniques d’accès à ces environnements et la coordination des incidents relevant de son périmètre.


Monthey Energies conservera la gouvernance du système d’information, la définition des priorités, la validation des décisions structurantes et la maîtrise des processus métier. Le titulaire prendra en charge les activités opérationnelles comprises dans le marché et proposera une organisation permettant d’assurer la qualité, la sécurité et la continuité des services.

title: Germany – Office block construction work – Vergabeverfahren zum Erwerb einer Neuen Zentrale der Deutschen Bundesbank
description: Die Deutsche Bundesbank (nachfolgend auch "Bundesbank" oder "Auftraggeberin" genannt) ist die Zentralbank der Bundesrepublik Deutschland. Sie hat Verfassungsrang als bundesunmittelbare juristische Person des öffentlichen Rechts und ist integraler Bestandteil des Europäischen Systems der Zentralbanken. Sie wirkt mit dem vorrangigen Ziel, die Preisstabilität zu gewährleisten, verwaltet die Währungsreserven, sorgt für die bankmäßige Abwicklung des Zahlungsverkehrs im Inland und Ausland und trägt zur Stabilität der Zahlungs- und Verrechnungssysteme bei. Ihre Zentrale befindet sich in Frankfurt am Main und steht für die Erfüllung dieser gesetzlichen Kernaufgaben sowie die öffentliche Wahrnehmung der Institution. Mit dem Ende der Nutzungsdauer der bisherigen Zentrale und einer interimistischen Unterbringung in angemieteten Flächen ergibt sich für die Bundesbank die Notwendigkeit, eine moderne, repräsentative und zukunftsfähige Liegenschaft für die künftige Zentrale der Bundesbank zu erwerben. Der Erwerb der Liegenschaft auf der Grundlage eines noch zu verhandelnden Grundstückskaufvertrages mit Bauverpflichtung (Bauträgervertrag mit endfälliger Zahlung zum Festpreis) (auch "Kaufvertrag" genannt) ist Gegenstand dieses Vergabeverfahrens. Der Grundstückskaufvertrag bedarf der notariellen Beurkundung. Es ist derzeit vorgesehen, dass die Zuschlagserteilung und die notarielle Beurkundung in unmittelbarem zeitlichen Zusammenhang erfolgen. Der Entwurf des Grundstückskaufvertrages wird den im Teilnahmewettbewerb ausgewählten Bietern von der Bundesbank als Verhandlungsgrundlage zur Verfügung gestellt. Ziel der Beschaffung ist die Bündelung der Arbeitsplätze der Zentrale in einer Liegenschaft und die Abbildung der in den Vergabeunterlagen beschriebenen Anforderungen und Funktionen in einem Ensemble, das architektonisch und funktional den besonderen Anforderungen der Bundesbank entspricht. Nach derzeitigem Stand sind die Anforderungen der Bundesbank in einem zusammenhängenden Gebäudeensemble umzusetzen. Eine Änderung dieser Anforderungen ist im Rahmen des Verhandlungsverfahrens möglich. In der Liegenschaft sind Flächen für verschiedene Sonderfunktionen zu integrieren. Hierzu zählen nach aktuellem Stand beispielsweise ein differenziertes Konferenz- und Besprechungsangebot, eine umfassende Betriebsgastronomie (einschließlich Vorstandsgastronomie), Flächen für Fahrbereitschaft und Logistik sowie Sicherheitszentralen. Es ist nicht ausgeschlossen, dass Sonderfunktionen im Rahmen des Verhandlungsverfahrens entfallen, geändert werden oder andere Sonderfunktionen hinzukommen. Zur Umsetzung der Anforderungen kommt sowohl ein Neubau als auch eine Kernsanierung eines bestehenden Gebäudes oder eine Kombination hieraus in Betracht. Die Abnahme und Übergabe der vertragsgemäß hergestellten Liegenschaft durch die Bundesbank muss nach aktueller Planung spätestens sieben Jahre nach Zuschlagserteilung erfolgen (Meilenstein). Die zeitlichen Vorgaben und die Meilensteine können sich im Laufe des Vergabeverfahrens ändern. Eine verbindliche Festlegung der zeitlichen Vorgaben ist im Laufe des Verhandlungsverfahrens für alle Meilensteine vorgesehen. Nach § 2 S. 2 des Gesetzes über die Deutsche Bundesbank hat die Bundesbank ihren Sitz in Frankfurt am Main. Das Auswahlgebiet, in welchem die verfahrensgegenständliche Liegenschaft liegen muss, ist das Stadtgebiet Frankfurt am Main mit der sicherheitsbedingten Ausnahme der Bereiche des Flughafenareals und der nahegelegenen Gateway Gardens (Gemarkung 0518). Das Auswahlgebiet ergibt sich aus der Unterlage Auswahlgebiet (Anlage 1) und ist bei der Wahl des Standortes zwingend einzuhalten. Bei Widersprüchen hinsichtlich des Auswahlgebietes zwischen der Beschreibung in den übrigen Vergabeunterlagen und Anlage 1 gilt Anlage 1 vorrangig. Werden Grundstücke und/oder Liegenschaften angeboten, die sich ganz oder teilweise außerhalb des Auswahlgebietes befinden, führt dies zum zwingenden Ausschluss des Teilnahmeantrages. Die Liegenschaft muss auf einem Grundstück im Auswahlgebiet hergestellt werden, über welches der Auftragnehmer nach Maßgabe der Vergabeunterlagen im Zuschlagsfall zur Erbringung der ausgeschriebenen Leistung rechtssicher verfügen und der Bundesbank Eigentum an dem zu bebauenden Grundstück frei von nicht übernommenen Belastungen nach Maßgabe der Vergabeunterlagen, insbesondere des Grundstückskaufvertrages und seiner Anlagen verschaffen kann. Der Grundstückskaufvertrag und die Anforderungen an das Grundstück sind Gegenstand der Vertragsverhandlungen in der Verhandlungsphase und können sich noch ändern. Von den Bewerbern bzw. den Bietern sind nach Maßgabe der Vergabeunterlagen Erklärungen zum Grundstück abzugeben, aus denen sich je nach Verfahrensstufe immer konkreter ergibt, ob das angebotene Grundstück die Anforderungen der Bundesbank erfüllt. Welche Unterlagen diesbezüglich mit dem Teilnahmeantrag einzureichen sind, ergibt sich aus der Checkliste der vom Bewerber einzureichenden Unterlagen, die mit den Vergabeunterlagen zur Verfügung gestellt wird. Die Liegenschaft mit der noch zu errichtenden oder umzubauenden Immobilie muss die Anforderungen der Bundesbank erfüllen, die in den Vergabeunterlagen, insbesondere der Funktionalen Leistungsbeschreibung, im Raum- und Funktionsprogramm sowie den jeweils näher definierten Ausstattungs- und Nutzungsvorgaben aufgeführt sind. Diese Unterlagen sind Gegenstand der Vergabeunterlagen, die ausschließlich den Bietern, die zur Abgabe eines Angebotes aufgefordert werden, zur Verfügung gestellt werden. Eine Änderung oder Konkretisierung der Anforderungen im Rahmen des Verhandlungsverfahrens ist möglich. Damit die Bewerber bewerten können, ob sie die Anforderungen - ggf. mit Konsortialpartnern und/oder Nachunternehmern und/oder Eignungsgebern erfüllen können, ist den Vergabeunterlagen zum Teilnahmewettbewerb eine Informative Leistungsbeschreibung beigefügt. Hierin sind ausgewählte wesentliche Anforderungen der Auftraggeberin aufgeführt.

title: Sweden – Hotel meeting and conference services – Utbildningsanläggningar
description: Försvarsmakten har behov av att kunna nyttja utbildningsanläggningar på specifika orter i Sverige. Då förbandens utbildningsplaner och logibehov är komplexa och kan variera är det av stor vikt att flexibla avtal med anläggningar på de geografiska orterna kan tecknas för att Försvarsmakten ska kunna utföra sin planerade verksamhet. Med utbildningsanläggningar avses logi, förplägnad (mat) och utbildningslokaler i antingen paket (Helpension eller dagpaket) eller möjlighet att själv plocka ihop ett paket. Avseende enbart förplägnad (mat) så har Försvarsmakten avtal för detta, i de fall som det inte finns avtalstäckning på ort efter att avtalsleverantör för förplägnadsavtalet har tillfrågats så kan Försvarsmakten komma att nyttja avtalsleverantör för detta avtal för förplägnad (mat).

title: Sweden – Tents – Beredskapstält

title: Sweden – Video-conferencing equipment – AV-Produkter och kringtjänster
description: Upphandlingen avser ramavtal för tillhandahållande av specialistkompetens inom audiovisuella (AV) lösningar och omfattar tjänster för planering, projektering, installation, konfigurering, driftsättning, service och teknisk support av FRA:s AV-miljöer.Leverantören ska tillhandahålla teknisk kompetens för genomförande av såväl mindre serviceinsatser som större installations- och förändringsarbeten. Uppdrag kan omfatta bland annat:projektering och teknisk utformning av AV-lösningar,projektledning och teknisk samordning av AV-relaterade uppdrag,installation och montering av AV-utrustning,konfigurering, programmering och driftsättning av AV-system,integration mellan olika AV-komponenter och angränsande tekniska system,felsökning, felavhjälpning och återställning av funktion,förebyggande och avhjälpande underhåll,teknisk rådgivning och stöd inför förändringar eller nyinstallationer,teknisk support till beställaren samt, vid behov, utbildning och överlämning av installerade lösningar.tillhandahållande av produkter och material. bortforsling av material, skräp, gammal hårdvara inom området på av FRA anvisade platser. Uppdrag kan avse exempelvis mötesrum, konferensrum, utbildningslokaler, ledningsrum och andra verksamhetslokaler där AV-utrustning används.Avrope sker utifrån faktiskt behov av specialistkompetens inom AV under kontraktstiden. Beställaren garanterar inga volymer. Leverantören ska tillhandahålla kompetens för såväl löpande service, teknisk support och felsökning som projektering, projektledning, installation, montering, konfigurering, programmering, driftsättning och teknisk samordning av AV-lösningar.

title: Sweden – Management holdings services – Tjänster för donationsstiftelser
description: Upphandlingen omfattar tjänster för donationsstiftelser så som administration, kapitalförvaltning och redovisning.

title: Sweden – Homedelivery of provisions – Reserverad upphandling - Inhandling och distribution av dagligvaror
description: Upphandlingsenheten Mora, Orsa, Älvdalen inbjuder till reserverad upphandling av tjänsten inhandling och distribution av dagligvaror till personer med beslut om bistånd enligt socialtjänstlagen samt till kommunala verksamheter inom Mora kommun. En leverantör kommer att antas. Planderad avtalstart 2027-02-01. Välkomna att ställa frågor via funktionen ”frågor & svar” och vi hoppas att ni är intresserade av att lämna anbud i denna upphandling.

title: NASA-White Sand Test Facility-WSTF DEMIL A Mixed Metals Term Contract
description: NASA White Sands Test Facility (WSTF) � DEMIL A Mixed Metals Term Contract Invitation for Bids (IFB): 3-1-QSC-T-27-001 Location: NASA White Sands Test Facility, 12600 NASA Road, Las Cruces, NM 88012 GSA Auctions Listing: https://www.gsaauctions.gov/auctions/preview/380420 IMPORTANT NOTICE: This auction requires the apparent high bidder to submit completed and signed certification(s) found in the "Documents" section and/or proof of licensing to the Sales Contracting Officer before the award is finalized. Requirements vary by auction. Property Description This Invitation for Bids (IFB) is for a Comprehensive Scrap Metal Collection, Removal, and Recycling Services Sale Term Contract at NASA White Sands Test Facility. The estimated annual quantity is 130 tons of mixed, unsegregated, and unprepared scrap iron and steel, including light and heavy steel. Scrap may contain ferrous and nonferrous attachments and other foreign materials. Submission of Bids Required Email Subject: Bid Submission for 3-1-QSC-T-27-001 (TC) Email Bid Submissions To: westzonesealedbids@gsa.gov Important Solicitation Dates IFB Issuance Date: 15 October 2026 Deadline for Questions: 09 November 2026 Bid Submission Deadline: 13 November 2026 � 5:00 PM Central Time Bid Opening: 17 November 2026 � 11:00 AM Central Time Anticipated Pre-Award Date: 20 November 2026 KEY REQUIREMENTS (READ CAREFULLY) MANDATORY Pre-Bid Site Inspection Required (See IFB Section 3.3). Bid submissions must include completed Appendix A and Standard Form 114 (SF 114). Performance Guarantee Required: $6,000.00. Pricing is based on a percentage of a published market index. The contractor shall furnish required insurance documentation prior to performance in accordance with IFB Section 7.2. All solicitation amendments must be acknowledged, if applicable. Failure to comply with applicable solicitation requirements may result in a bid being deemed nonresponsive. Mandatory Pre-Bid Site Inspection (IFB Section 3.3) SITE ACCESS / SECURITY NASA White Sands Test Facility is a secured Federal installation. Advance coordination is required for all site access. Badging and access controls apply, and additional security restrictions may be enforced. All mandatory pre-bid site inspections must be scheduled and coordinated with the Government representatives identified below. Site Points of Contact (POCs): Pedro "Pete" Rios Email: pete.rios-1@nasa.gov Mobile: 575-779-6149 Office: 575-524-5138 Johnny J. Bernal Email: johnny.j.bernal@nasa.gov Mobile: 575-649-5284 Office: 575-524-5140 Solicitation Documents and Questions All solicitation documents, including the IFB, Surveillance Plan, and Appendices, are available in the Documents section of the GSA Auctions listing: https://www.gsaauctions.gov/auctions/preview/380420 Prospective bidders are responsible for reviewing the complete IFB, all applicable attachments, and any amendments before submitting a bid. All questions must be submitted in writing before the deadline identified in the IFB. Email Bid Questions To: alfonso.brown@gsa.gov Sales Contracting Officer (SCO) Alfonso L. Brown Sr. General Services Administration (GSA) Email: alfonso.brown@gsa.gov Phone: 817-978-0771
